newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees faster growth in 97, says 12 meet EMU test.
newsitem.headline: EU sees faster growth in 97, says 12 meet EMU test.

text.p: Economic growth in the European Union is expected to advance at a rate of 1.7 percent in 1996, rising further to 2.3 percent in 1997, the European Commission said on Wednesday.

In its twice-yearly review of economic conditions in the 15-nation bloc, the EU's executive also said 12 countries are expected to bring their deficits down to at least 3.0 percent of gross domestic product in 1997.
Countries wishing to join a single currency in 1999 must meet a series of economic tests in 1997, among which are relatively tight budget policies.
By the Commission's calculations, only Greece, Italy and Britain are seen not meeting the Maastricht treaty's deficit criteria.
On the economic front, the Commission's estimates for growth in the EU were little changed from its last forecast in the spring.

At that time, the Commission saw GDP rising at a rate of 1.5 percent in 1996, followed by a 2.4 percent pickup next year. For Germany, the EU's economic powerhouse, economic growth was revised sharply upward in 1996, from 0.5 percent to 1.4 percent. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
